paper.title: JARVIS-Leaderboard: a large scale benchmark of materials design methods
paper.research_summary: JARVIS-Leaderboard is an open-source, community-driven platform for benchmarking and enhancing reproducibility in materials science. It integrates computational, experimental, and data-analytics methods across five categories—Artificial Intelligence (AI), Electronic Structure (ES), Force-fields (FF), Quantum Computation (QC), and Experiments (EXP)—and supports multiple data modalities (atomic structures, spectra, images, text). The platform hosts 274 benchmarks, 152 methods, 1281 contributions, and over 8 million data points, enabling systematic, transparent, and unbiased validation of materials design approaches.

tasks.objective: to provide a comprehensive, reproducible, transparent, and unbiased framework for benchmarking materials design methods across multiple categories and data modalities
constraints: must be based on well-characterized/well-known samples/tasks with digital object identifier/peer-reviewed article links
must include run script to exactly reproduce results
must include metadata file with team name, contact information, computational timing and software/hardware used
input_requirements: reference benchmark data (e.g., experimental data, DFT data, analytical results)
user-submitted method outputs (e.g., predictions, measurements, simulations)
output_goal: performance rankings across methods for each benchmark
reproducible, comparable, and interpretable evaluation metrics (e.g., MAE, accuracy, ROUGE)

evidence.text: This work introduces JARVIS-Leaderboard, an open-source and community-driven platform that facilitates benchmarking and enhances reproducibility.
The goal of this project is to provide a more comprehensive framework for materials benchmarking than previous works.

evidence.text: These test identiﬁers (such as JVASP-1408) must match the test set ids in the json.zip ﬁle in the benchmarks folder for the metric measurements to work.

We use several metrics in the leaderboard depending on the “sub-categories” mentioned above. We use mean absolute error (MAE), accuracy (acc), multi-mae (L1 norm of multi-dimensional data), recall-oriented understudy for gisting evaluation (ROUGE) for the single property prediction, single property classiﬁcation, spectra/eigensolver/atomic forces and textGen/text summary subcategories respectively.

stages.stage_goal: to verify contribution reproducibility and correctness before public release
stage_output: verified contribution ready for pull request

evidence.text: The contributions can be locally checked by the user using jarvis_serve.py script.

This script automatically forks the parent usnistgov/jarvis_leaderboard repo for the user, adds the team-name folder with its ﬁles in that forked repo, runs a few minimal sanity checks on the new contribution, and then makes a pull request to the parent repo. The contribution addition and automated testings are carried out using GitHub actions.

stages.stage_goal: to ensure benchmark trustworthiness and methodological rigor through expert review
stage_output: validated contribution integrated into leaderboard website

evidence.text: The administrators of the JARVIS-Leaderboard at NIST will verify the contributions and then ﬁnally, it will become part of the leaderboard website.

A new benchmark must be associated with a peer-reviewed article and a DOI, in order to have trust in the reference benchmark data. A new benchmark must also be veriﬁed by the JARVIS-Leaderboard administrators.

The user can populate the reference dataset (with well-deﬁned data splits) used for a speciﬁc benchmark (e.g., for 2D exfoliation energies in JARVIS-DFT dataset using an AI method: “AI-SinglePropertyPrediction-exfoliation_energy-dft_3d-test”).

In each of these sub-folders, there are .json.zip ﬁles with well-deﬁned reference datasets and available properties as also available in the JARVIS-Tools package https://pages.nist.gov/jarvis/databases/.

For entries in the AI category, the data is in train-validation-test splits (using a ﬁxed random number generator). For the current leaderboard format, we report the performance accuracy in the test set only. These ﬁles can be easily edited with common text editors. Each contribution folder (e.g. alignn-model) consists of one or several csv.zip ﬁles corresponding to each benchmark (such as for formation energies, bandgap, etc.).

The components are the categories (such as AI), sub-categories (such as ImageClass), property (such as bravais_lattice), dataset-name (such as stem_2d_image as available in the JARVIS-Tools database page), and data-split.

Note that these datasets contain all varieties of data modalities, such as atomic structure, images, spectra, and text. We ﬁnd that the most common elements are C, N, O, Cu, which is similar to the natural abundance of these elements.
